title: Flipbooks, @function, Blend Text, Lasso & Bubbles
description: Five live UI drops: hold-time-weighted mascot flipbook animation, native CSS @function fluid layouts, blend-mode canvas text, vector lasso multi-select, and a floating text-selection bubble menu.

drops.title: Mascot Flipbook Timeline
drops.description: Three original SVG mascots animated purely through hand-tuned hold-time weighting on each pose — no tweening at all.
drops.concept: Reimplements the mechanism behind expressive mascot/brand animation: instead of interpolating between states, a sequence of discrete poses is displayed in order, and the perceived weight comes entirely from how long each pose is held. Key poses (the bottom of a squat, the top of a lift) hold 3-5x longer than transitional poses, which reads as intentional, weighted motion despite zero easing curves. A toggle lets you flatten every hold to the same duration to feel exactly what that timing removes.
drops.source: Inspired by Codrops' (Ayotomiwa Wale-Durojaye) "Reverse-Engineering Claude AI's Mascot Animations with SVG and GSAP"

interaction.mouse: Play/pause each mascot, scrub the frame timeline, toggle equalized holds
interaction.click: Click a timeline tick to jump to that pose
interaction.touch: All controls are touch-friendly buttons and sliders

drops.title: CSS @function Fluid System
drops.description: A dashboard where every padding, radius, gap and column count is computed by native CSS @function rules, not JS or Sass.
drops.concept: The @function at-rule (Chrome 139+) lets you define a real, reusable, typed CSS function with a result: statement, callable anywhere a value is expected. A --fluid-space() function clamps padding/gaps between a min and max based on the panel's live width, and an --auto-cols() function branches on a container query to switch column counts — both driven purely by custom properties, with a JS fallback that recomputes the identical formula when @function isn't supported.
drops.source: Inspired by Una Kravets (Chrome DevRel), "5 Useful CSS functions using the new @function rule"

interaction.mouse: Drag the panel's right edge to resize; tune sliders for padding/columns
interaction.touch: Drag handle supports touch via Pointer Events

drops.title: Blend-Mode Canvas Text
drops.description: Giant headline text filled with a living animated canvas pattern via mix-blend-mode alone — no video, no background-clip.
drops.concept: A full-bleed canvas paints an animated pattern (plasma, particle swarm, or a synthetic audio-reactive waveform) behind text set in the exact same color as the canvas's base fill. With mix-blend-mode: screen (or multiply/difference), the browser combines the two layers pixel-for-pixel, so the pattern only becomes visible where the glyph shapes are — everywhere else the text blends invisibly into the matching background.
drops.source: Technique popularized by Dudley Storey's canonical blend-mode text CodePen demo

interaction.mouse: n/a — purely visual, tune via the panel
interaction.click: Change pattern, blend mode, text and speed in the panel

drops.title: Vector Lasso Select
drops.description: Drag a rectangle across 60 color swatches to multi-select them, modeled as a signed vector instead of a plain width/height box.
drops.concept: Represents the drag gesture as a DOMVector — an origin point plus a signed magnitudeX/magnitudeY — instead of a rectangle, since a drag can go in any of four directions from its anchor and a naive width/height model breaks when dragging left or up. A toDOMRect() helper normalizes the vector into a real rect via Math.min/Math.abs, and every candidate item is intersection-tested against it with a standard AABB overlap check, with edge auto-scroll via requestAnimationFrame.
drops.source: Inspired by Joshua Wootonn, "Drag to Select"

interaction.mouse: Drag to lasso-select; Shift/Cmd-drag to add to selection
interaction.click: Click a swatch to toggle it; Esc clears all
interaction.touch: Drag works with touch via Pointer Events

drops.title: Floating Selection Bubble Menu
drops.description: Select any text in the article and a formatting toolbar appears right above it, flipping below when there's no room.
drops.concept: Listens for the selectionchange event; whenever window.getSelection() is non-collapsed, range.getBoundingClientRect() gives the selection's screen position, and a toolbar is absolutely positioned centered above it, flipping below when too close to the viewport top. The detail most clones miss: toolbar buttons must bind mousedown (not click) with preventDefault(), or the browser collapses the text selection before the click ever fires.

interaction.mouse: Select text to summon the bubble; click a button to format
interaction.touch: Long-press to select text on touch devices
